scenes.label: Meet the team
scenes.title: The glowing mosaic
scenes.caption: Nikhil builds a mosaic for Reva’s imaginary museum. Each square stores grayscale brightness from 0 to 255, with larger values brighter. The grid records measurements; it cannot establish a doorway interpretation.
scenes.speech: Nikhil builds a mosaic for Reva’s imaginary museum. Each square stores grayscale brightness from 0 to 255, with larger values brighter. The grid records measurements; it cannot establish a doorway interpretation.
scenes.dialogue: A stored value is an observation.

scenes.label: The problem
scenes.title: 8 places for brightness
scenes.caption: A sample square has brightness 173. Its binary places are 128, 64, 32, 16, 8, 4, 2 and 1. Reva selects places adding to the supplied value. The resulting bits encode a number, rather than meaning.
scenes.speech: A sample square has brightness 173. Its binary places are 128, 64, 32, 16, 8, 4, 2 and 1. Reva selects places adding to the supplied value. The resulting bits encode a number, rather than meaning.
scenes.dialogue: Bits encode the number, not its meaning.

scenes.label: How it works
scenes.title: A visible stripe
scenes.caption: The first 3 by 3 image has a bright centre column and dark pixels elsewhere. Nikhil’s rule detects a stripe only when every centre pixel is bright. This checks positions, rather than proving the picture contains a doorway.
scenes.speech: The first 3 by 3 image has a bright centre column and dark pixels elsewhere. Nikhil’s rule detects a stripe only when every centre pixel is bright. This checks positions, rather than proving the picture contains a doorway.
scenes.dialogue: Write what the rule actually checks.

scenes.label: Your decision
scenes.title: Move the same pattern
scenes.caption: Reva shifts the bright stripe left without changing its shape. The centre column becomes dark. Choose whether the original rule still detects it. A human may describe the shifted pattern as similar while the rule returns differently.
scenes.speech: Reva shifts the bright stripe left without changing its shape. The centre column becomes dark. Choose whether the original rule still detects it. A human may describe the shifted pattern as similar while the rule returns differently.
scenes.dialogue: Similar to us may differ to a rule.

scenes.label: What changes
scenes.title: Observation and interpretation
scenes.caption: The notebook separates observing bright centre pixels from interpreting them as a doorway. Only the observation follows directly from the supplied numbers. The interpretation needs context, a definition and comparisons with pictures that could produce the same feature.
scenes.speech: The notebook separates observing bright centre pixels from interpreting them as a doorway. Only the observation follows directly from the supplied numbers. The interpretation needs context, a definition and comparisons with pictures that could produce the same feature.
scenes.dialogue: Do not smuggle a story into a pixel.

scenes.label: Enter the lab
scenes.title: Keep a feature record
scenes.caption: In the lab, encode brightness, mark the original feature and test the shifted input. Record where the rule fails. This experiment demonstrates a representation limit; it does not show that every image model behaves identically or understands every picture.
scenes.speech: In the lab, encode brightness, mark the original feature and test the shifted input. Record where the rule fails. This experiment demonstrates a representation limit; it does not show that every image model behaves identically or understands every picture.
scenes.dialogue: Test the claim under a change.
